_note: Ground truth read directly from the client's four PDFs by a human-equivalent read of the pages named. Page numbers are PDF page numbers, matching what the system reports. Nothing here is inferred; every line was seen on the page cited. doc16's printed folio runs 3 lower than its PDF page (PDF 21 = printed 'Page 18 of 46') - the PDF number is authoritative here because that is what the system cites.

facts.question: What size must design submittal drawings be?
facts.quote: Design submittal drawings shall be ANSI-D size (22 X 34), suitable for half-size (11" x 17") scaled reproduction.

facts.question: What is the smallest mechanical piping that must be modelled?
facts.quote: All piping 1-1/2" NPS and larger shall be modeled.

facts.question: What scale governs model granularity?
facts.quote: at a minimum must include all features that would be included on a quarter inch (1/4" = 1'0") scaled drawing

facts.question: Which IFC Coordination View must the software be certified in?
facts.quote: must be certified in the IFC Coordination View (2x3 or better)

facts.question: Which document governs minimum BIM submittal requirements for New York District projects?
facts.quote: the requirements of Attachment F shall govern and the contents of Part 2 of this Manual should be considered informational only

facts.question: What design percentage is a draft submission from the BIM Pit?
facts.quote: a substantially complete master model with extractions and sheet files comprising a draft submission (usually at least a 50% design submission)

facts.question: What are the minimum structural model requirements?
facts.quote: 4.4 Structural ... 4.4.1 Foundations. 4.4.2 Floor Slabs. 4.4.3 Structural Steel. 4.4.4 Cast-in-Place Concrete. 4.4.5 Expansion/Contraction Joints. 4.4.6 Stairs.
facts.trap: These belong to Section 4 (BIM Model Minimum Requirements), NOT to Section 3.3.1 (Interim Design Submittals). A previous live run attributed foundations to interim submittals. Any answer that calls these an interim-submittal requirement is WRONG.

facts.question: What must interim design submittals include?
facts.quote: 3.3.1 BIM and CAD Detail. The Model shall include architectural, interior design, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection systems and Facility Data, as applicable to the Interim Design package(s).
facts.trap: This clause lists DISCIPLINES, not building elements. An answer naming foundations or floor slabs here has confused Section 3.3.1 with Section 4.4.

facts.question: What are the three parts of a design analysis?
facts.quote: The design analysis will be organized into three parts; Part 1 - "General Description," Part 2 - "Design Requirements and Provisions," and Part 3 - "O&M Provisions."

facts.question: What units must a design analysis use and what standard governs conversions?
facts.quote: Unit designations and conversions shall be in accordance with ASTM E 621-84 as modified by the Metric Guide for Federal Construction

facts.question: Which design disciplines does Part 2 of a design analysis cover?
facts.quote: (1) Civil. (2) Environmental. (3) Architectural. (4) Structural. (5) Mechanical. (6) Electrical. (7) Fire Protection and Life Safety. (8) Physical Security.
facts.trap: Part 2 lists EIGHT disciplines and does NOT include communications or HTRW. The Part 1 list on the same page does mention communications and HTRW aspects. Attributing the Part 1 list to Part 2 is WRONG.

facts.question: What page size must design analysis materials use?
facts.quote: a vertically oriented A4 metric, 210 mm x 297 mm (8.3 inches x 11.7 inches) standard page size

facts.question: How long must a reference copy of the design analysis be retained?
facts.quote: Reference copies of the design analysis will be retained by the design agency for at least two years after the beneficial occupancy date (BOD) of the project.

facts.question: How many sections does Part 1 of the design analysis comprise?
facts.quote: The design analysis -Part 1- will comprise five (5) sections with subsections

comparisons.question: compare design requirements in doc13.pdf, doc15.pdf and doc16.pdf
comparisons.note: A named-document comparison must not pull passages from unrelated textbooks. A previous live run surfaced a professional-practices book and a differential-equations textbook in the claim table for this exact question.

comparisons.question: compare design submittal percentages in doc13.pdf and doc16.pdf
comparisons.note: doc13 p.125 carries '16.2 Concept/early Preliminary (35%) Design Submittal'; doc16 p.18 carries 'usually at least a 50% design submission'. A previous live run reported this as a POSSIBLE GAP with 'none cited' on the project side, which is a FALSE GAP - doc16 does speak to it. Both sides must be found.

comparisons.question: compare structural model requirements in doc16.pdf and doc15.pdf
comparisons.note: A previous live run answered a structural-models question with a differential-equations textbook passage ('which of the following models would produce very accurate results'), matching on the bare word 'models'.

facet_rules.description: No facet name may be or contain a bare unit or symbol token such as '%' or '(%)'.
No facet name may be a bare numeral or clause number alone.
A facet name must read as a noun phrase, not a bag of query words in arbitrary order.
Two facets whose term sets are subset-related and share a head noun must be one facet.
A facet with no claims on either side must not be emitted.
